notes: Mitchell, Wagner and Veilleux, SIR 2023-5014 (no revisions listed): ten flood regions (figs. 2-6) at 8 AEPs (0.2-50 percent), fitted with WREG. Equations, AVP, SEPavg, model error variance and the number of streamgages from Table 5 (pp. 30-32); ranges from Table 6 (p. 33). Every equation is Q = 10^b0 times a product of powers, so intercept = b0 as printed and every variable is log10. Region 10 (southern Island of Hawaii) uses I48H500Y alone, with no drainage area; region 3's PRECIP and PERM24IN at 0.2 percent, region 4's I60M25Y at 0.2-2 percent, region 7's DRNAREA at 50 percent and region 8's PRECIP at 0.2-1 percent are printed in bold italics (not statistically significant) and are stored as printed. Variable codes are NSS's: DRNAREA (mi2), PRECIP (mean annual precipitation, in.), PERM24IN (area-weighted soil permeability of the top 24 in., in./hr), I60M25Y (60-minute, 25-year precipitation, in.), I48H500Y (48-hour, 500-year precipitation, in.). sep_log is Table 5's SEPavg percent converted as sqrt(ln(1 + (SEP/100)^2)) / ln(10); avp is Table 5's AVP; model_error_variance is Table 5's MEV (region 6 prints 0.000 at 0.2-2 percent, stored as 0). The report prints no covariance matrix (X^T Lambda^-1 X)^-1 (appendix 4 gives site variances of prediction for gaged sites only), so covariance is not stored and intervals use sep_log. n_sites is Table 5's streamgage count per region (17, 16, 43, 26, 12, 9, 15, 40, 30, 9). The report's Student's t uses n - k degrees of freedom with k the number of explanatory variables (region 1: 17 gages, 2 variables, t = 2.1314 at 15), one more than the n - k - 1 flowfreq uses, so a stored interval's t is slightly larger than the printed one (2.1448 against 2.1314 for region 1; the difference shrinks with n). Checks: Tables 5 and 6 were entered from the rendered pages.
